title: arXiv Mathematics — 13 November 2026: 9 notable papers
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart. This ordering is inferred from mathematical claims, scope, and corroborating signals; independent-attention and citation evidence is sparse for papers this recent, so the list is notable recent mathematics rather than measured popularity.

sections.title: GFF for 3D Ising interfaces in three moves of Tetris
sections.abstract: The authors establish a Gaussian free field scaling limit for tilted interfaces in the three-dimensional Ising model at sufficiently low temperature, through reductions to SOS, half-monotone SOS, and dimer models.
sections.claimed_result: The abstract and Theorem 1 claim local gradient convergence and, after rescaling, convergence modulo constants to an anisotropic Gaussian free field for positive slopes and sufficiently large inverse temperature; analogous limits are claimed for SOS and half-monotone SOS.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: 3D Ising model on tilted tori, strictly positive limiting slopes, and inverse temperature above a threshold; amplitude and anisotropy depend on temperature and slope.
sections.unique_caveat: Restricted to low temperature and positive slopes; the fluctuation amplitude and linear anisotropy map are not explicit.

sections.title: The loop-ensemble scaling limits of near-critical percolation in the plane
sections.abstract: For near-critical site percolation on the triangular lattice at fixed nonzero parameter, the author proves a unique scaling limit for all cluster-boundary loops and convergence of exploration paths to continuous paths.
sections.claimed_result: Theorem 1.2 claims convergence in law of the near-critical loop ensemble in loop-ensemble space for each fixed λ ≠ 0; the introduction also states convergence in distribution of near-critical exploration paths to continuous paths.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Site percolation on the triangular lattice, near-critical parameter fixed and nonzero, mesh tending to zero; based on established quad-crossing scaling limits.
sections.unique_caveat: The result is for the specified triangular-lattice near-critical coupling, not arbitrary planar percolation models.

sections.title: A complete solution to the Naor isomorphic reverse isoperimetry conjecture
sections.abstract: For every origin-symmetric convex body, the authors claim a volume-preserving linear transformation and a nearby symmetric convex body with isoperimetric quotient at most 40 ε⁻¹√n, resolving Naor's conjecture.
sections.claimed_result: Theorem 1.1 claims that for each origin-symmetric convex body K⊂Rⁿ there is T∈SLₙ(R) such that for every 0<ε<1 there is symmetric L with (1−ε)TK⊆L⊆TK and iq(L)≤40 ε⁻¹√n.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Finite-dimensional real space; K is an origin-symmetric convex body and T preserves volume.
sections.unique_caveat: The bound concerns nearby L inside transformed K, not the quotient of TK itself; preprint proof not independently checked.

sections.title: The Pólya–Szegő buckling conjecture in dimensions two through forty-seven
sections.abstract: The authors prove the Pólya–Szegő conjecture for dimensions 2 through 47: among open sets of fixed finite volume, a ball minimizes the first clamped buckling eigenvalue, with a sharp comparison to the first Dirichlet eigenvalue.
sections.claimed_result: For 2≤n≤47, the abstract claims Λ₁(Ω)≥(j_{n/2,1}/j_{n/2−1,1})² λ₁ᴰ(Ω), with balls as volume-constrained minimizers and equality characterized up to sets of zero H² capacity.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Open sets of prescribed finite volume; Λ₁ is the first clamped buckling eigenvalue and λ₁ᴰ the first Dirichlet eigenvalue.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem covers dimensions 2–47 only; the authors' calibration fails at n≥48, without disproving the conjecture there.

sections.title: Forbidden subset sums in a linear range: an inverse theorem and the Erdős-Graham irregularity problem
sections.abstract: The paper gives an inverse theorem for dense sets with forbidden subset sums and derives an exact formula for c≥1 and non-convergence and subsequential limits for the Erdős–Graham extremal function when 0<c<1.
sections.claimed_result: Claims f_c(n)=⌊cn⌋−⌈n/2⌉ for c≥1; for 0<c<1 it proves non-convergence, limsup c/2, and further limits under least-non-divisor conditions. The inverse theorem applies when 2^(q−2)E≤sT; selected results are Lean-verified.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: f_c(n) maximizes the size of a subset of {1,…,⌊cn⌋} avoiding n as a sum of distinct elements; inverse theorem has additional size and arithmetic hypotheses.
sections.unique_caveat: The full limit-point set is identified only for c=1/2 in the abstract; the subsequential formula is conditional and formal verification covers specified portions.

sections.title: The Fourier dimension conjecture for complex Gaussian multiplicative chaos on the circle
sections.abstract: The author proves the Bonnefont–Rajamäki–Vargas Fourier-dimension conjecture throughout its stated parameter range for complex Gaussian multiplicative chaos on the circle, with additional boundary decay and Sobolev results.
sections.claimed_result: For the canonical holomorphic family the claimed dimension identity holds almost surely on the stated open parameter regions; on the specified sloping boundary, Fourier coefficients decay logarithmically and the Fourier dimension is zero.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Complex Gaussian multiplicative chaos built from a single real Gaussian field on the circle, with γ=α+iβ in stated parameter regions.
sections.unique_caveat: The identity is proved on the conjecture's stated parameter range, not all complex parameters; boundary behavior differs from the interior formula.

sections.title: Existence of a fluid phase for the two-dimensional one-component plasma
sections.abstract: For inverse temperature β≤2, the authors claim exponential correlation decay and uniqueness within a controlled-fluctuation class, yielding an infinite-volume plasma process and first-order Debye–Hückel asymptotics.
sections.claimed_result: The abstract claims exponential correlation decay and uniqueness for β≤2 in the stated class, constructs Gin_β, and identifies the truncated two-point function to first order in β at the Debye-length scale.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Two-dimensional logarithmically repelling point charges in a neutralizing background; β≤2 and stated fluctuation-control condition for uniqueness.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract does not establish the fluid phase or uniqueness beyond β=2.

sections.title: The coercivity conjecture for nonlocal energies
sections.abstract: The authors disprove the implication from uniform ellipticity to fractional Sobolev coercivity for symmetric nonlocal kernels when n>2s, prove it for n=1, s>1/2, and give criteria for important kernel classes.
sections.claimed_result: Claims failure for n>2s, including smooth compactly supported tests, a positive result for n=1, s>1/2, and a local coercivity criterion based on annular cancellation.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Symmetric nonlocal kernels of order 2s, 0<s<1, with stated ellipticity conditions; positive results require additional cancellation or class-specific hypotheses.
sections.unique_caveat: Does not settle all remaining dimension/order and kernel combinations.

sections.title: A counterexample to fixed-profile soliton resolution for the three-dimensional quintic wave equation
sections.abstract: The authors construct a bounded global solution of the focusing energy-critical 3D wave equation whose core approaches distinct stationary profiles along different times, contradicting fixed-profile soliton resolution in the stated setting.
sections.claimed_result: Claims a bounded forward-global solution asymptotic to a varying stationary profile plus one free wave, with two limits in distinct similarity orbits that rule out a fixed profile list in the asserted resolution form.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Focusing energy-critical quintic wave equation in three spatial dimensions; solution starts arbitrarily close to a sign-changing stationary state.
sections.unique_caveat: A constructed counterexample in a specified equation and near a specified stationary state; it does not classify all energy-critical wave asymptotics.
